recipes.title: Ginataang Bangus
recipes.description: Fried milkfish cooked in coconut milk with shrimp paste, ginger, garlic, and Thai chili.
ingredients: 8 pieces string beans cut into 2-inch lengths
fish sauce and ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Season the bangus with Maggi Magic Sarap.
Dredge the fish in all-purpose flour, making sure it is evenly coated. Set aside.
Heat the cooking oil in a pan. Fry the bangus until both sides turn light to medium brown. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Using 2 tablespoons of the oil from frying the fish, stir-fry the string beans for about 90 seconds. Remove and set aside.
Add another 2 tablespoons of oil to the pan. Sauté the garlic until it starts to brown, then add the onion and ginger. Continue cooking until the onion softens.
Add the shrimp paste and Thai chili peppers. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Pour in the coconut milk and let it come to a boil.
Add the fried bangus and string beans. Lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and ground black pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Lechon Kawali
recipes.description: Juicy and tender pork while the skin is brown and crispy with a good combination of taste and texture in every bite.
instructions: Boil water in a cooking pot.
Add whole peppercorn, bay leaves, and Knorr Pork Cube. Stir.
Add the pork belly. Cover the pot and continue to boil in medium heat for 45 minutes. You can add more water if needed.
Remove the pork belly from the cooking pot and place in a clean plate. Let it cool down.
Rub Knorr liquid seasoning all over the boiled pork belly. Let it stay for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep cooking pot. Once the oil gets hot enough (300F), gently put the pork belly into the pot. Deep-fry the pork in medium heat for 7 to 10 minutes.
Turn the pork belly over. Continue to fry the opposite side for 8 minutes or until the skin gets crisp and brown.
Remove the crispy deep fried pork belly from the cooking pot. Arrange in a plate with wire rack or paper towel. Let it cool down. Slice the pork into serving pieces.
Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with your favorite sauce.

recipes.title: Filipino Style Pork BBQ
recipes.description: Composed of thinly sliced pork pieces that are marinated in a special mixture of seasonings and spices.
ingredients: 4 lbs. pork shoulder sliced into thin pieces
½ cup juice extracted from calamansi or lemon
1 ½ cups lemon or lime soda
instructions: Arrange the pork slices in a large bowl.
Add all the marinade ingredients. Mix well. Cover the bowl and marinate for at least 3 hours.
Fasten the marinated pork together using bamboo skewers.
Heat-up the grill. Start to grill your Filipino Style pork BBQ for 3 to 5 minutes per side until the meat is thoroughly cooked. Make sure to always baste the BBQ when flipping it over.
Serve with spicy vinegar.

recipes.title: Beef Kaldereta
recipes.description: A Filipino beef stew cooked in tomato sauce with liver spread.
ingredients: salt and ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine the beef and soy sauce in a bowl. Mix well and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the cooking oil in a large pot or pressure cooker. Sauté the garlic and onion until fragrant, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the marinated beef. Cook while stirring for 3 to 5 minutes, or until the meat turns light brown on all sides.
Pour in the tomato sauce and beef broth. Add the dried bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat. Cover and cook until the beef becomes tender.
Add the carrots, potatoes, and green olives. Stir to combine.
Add the liver spread and chili flakes. Continue cooking for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.
Add the red and green bell peppers. Cook for about 3 minutes.
Season with salt and ground black pepper to taste.
Serve hot with steamed white rice.

recipes.title: Beef Mechado
recipes.description: A colorful and vibrant dish that can liven up your kitchen table.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a pan then saute the garlic and onion.
Put-in the beef and saute for about 3 minutes or until color turns light brown.
Add the tomato sauce and water then simmer until the meat is tender. Add water as needed.
Add the soy sauce, ground black pepper, lemon rind, laurel leaves, and salt then simmer until excess liquid evaporates.
Put-in the potatoes and cook until the potatoes are soft.
Place in a serving plate then serve hot with rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Inasal
recipes.description: A grilled chicken dish from the Western Visayas region.
instructions: Combine all the brine ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat and stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
Transfer the hot brine to a large mixing bowl, add the ice cubes, and stir. Let the mixture cool down completely.
Soak the chicken in the brine solution for 90 minutes. Drain the liquid and set the chicken aside.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine all the marinade ingredients. Mix well. Add the chicken and marinate for 3 hours.

Grill the chicken until the internal temperature reaches 165F. Baste it with the marinade for the first few minutes of grilling, and finish it by brushing with a combination of chicken oil and margarine all over.
Remove the grilled chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve with rice, pickled papaya, and a dipping sauce of sinamak (spiced vinegar).

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.description: A stir fry with thin slices of beef and broccoli florets in a brown sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb beef sliced into thin pieces
instructions: Combine all the sauce ingredients in a bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
Combine the beef with all the marinade ingredients in a bowl. Mix until the beef is evenly coated. Let it sit for at least 10 minutes.

Heat 1 tablespoon of cooking oil in a wok or pan over high heat. Stir fry the broccoli for 30 seconds. Pour in 2 tablespoons of water, cover the pan, and steam the broccoli for 1 minute. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Heat the remaining cooking oil in the same pan over high heat. Fry the marinated beef for about 40 to 90 seconds per side or until lightly browned.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the broccoli to the pan and toss to combine with the beef.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Gently stir and cook over medium high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and broccoli.
Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Pork Siomai
ingredients: 2 sachets Knorr SavorRich Pork Seasoning 44g each
instructions: Combine ground pork and minced shrimp in a bowl. Gradually mix together.
Add jicama, carrot, onion, scallion, egg, ground black pepper, and sesame oil. Continue to mix until all the ingredients are well blended.
Add Knorr SavorRich Pork Liquid Seasoning. Mix well.
Scoop 1 1/2 tablespoons of the pork mixture and wrap in wonton wrapper. Perform this step until the mixture is fully consumed.
Arrange in a steamer and then steam for 15 to 20 minutes.
Transfer to a serving plate. Serve with toyo and calamansi dipping sauce and some chili garlic paste.

recipes.title: Pork Chao Fan
recipes.description: A flavorful and filling meal consists of a chewy, delicious pork belly and rice.
ingredients: 6 ounces ground pork or grilled pork belly
Salt and ground white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat oil in a wok. Add beaten eggs. Fry until eggs are fully cooked. Remove eggs from the pan. Set aside.
Sauté onion using remaining oil until it softens.
Add ground pork. Cook while stirring until pork turns medium brown.
Pour soy sauce, Sesame oil, and hoisin sauce into the wok. Stir.
Add carrots and leftover rice. Stir-fry for 2 minutes. Toss until all ingredients are well distributed.
Add green peas and green onions. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped fried egg and then season with salt and ground white pepper.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Pork Dumplings
recipes.description: Rice wraps filled with ground pork, ginger, garlic, and cabbage, then steamed.
instructions: Mash the cabbage. Add salt. Continue to mash until salt is well distributed. Let it stay for 10 minutes.
Combine ground pork, shrimp, ginger, and chives in bowl. Mix well.
Add cabbage, ground white pepper, cooking wine, Sesame oil, and Knorr liquid seasoning. Continue to mix until all ingredients are well blended.
Scoop 1 ½ teaspoon of pork mixture and place it in the middle of the Gyoza wrapper. Secure the filling by symmetrically folding the wrapper and pressing the edges.
Arrange the pork dumplings on a steamer lined with cabbage leaves. Cover and steam for 10 minutes.
Serve with dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Siopao Asado
recipes.description: A type of dumpling with a sweet pork filling.
ingredients: 2 ½ tablespoons sugar added to yeast mixture
½ cup sugar added to the flour mixture
2 lbs pork chopped into small pieces
2 tablespoons cornstarch diluted in 1/4 cup water
instructions: Cook the Asado filling by heating the shortening in a pan.
Saute the garlic and onions.
Put-in the pork and cook until the color of the outer part turns light brown.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin sauce, and sugar then mix well. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Put in the corn starch (diluted in water) and mix until the texture of the sauce becomes thick. Set aside.
Make the dough by placing warm water in a bowl then add the yeast and sugar and mix well. Leave the mixture for 10 to 15 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, put-in the flour, baking powder, shortening (or lard), and the yeast-sugar-water mixture then mix well.
Knead the combined mixture until the texture of the dough becomes fine. Let the dough rise by setting it aside for at least an hour.
Knead the dough again then cut into individual slices.
Flatten the dough until a round shape is formed using a rolling pin.
Put the asado filling on the middle of the flattened dough and wrap.
Place the siopao in a steamer and steam for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with siopao sauce.

recipes.title: Spicy Wonton Soup
recipes.description: Small dumplings filled with meat or veggies and wrapped in a thin dough.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons chili oil with garlic and chili
instructions: Pour water in a cooking pot. Let boil.
Add the pork neck bones and medium chopped onion. Continue to boil between low to medium heat for 1 ½ hours.
Meanwhile, prepare the wonton by combining all the wonton ingredients in a bowl (except the wrapper). Mix well.

Scoop 2 teaspoons of pork mixture and arrange it in the middle of the wrapper. Seal by folding the wrapper in a way that both ends meet together forming a triangular shape. Press against the side of the wonton to ensure that it remains intact. Set aside.
Remove the pork neck bones from the pot. Set it aside.
Add 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and ½ teaspoon ground black pepper in the cooking pot. Stir.
Add the noodles and wonton into the pot. Let the liquid re-boil. Continue to cook 8 minutes.
Add the scallions and half of the chili oil and toasted garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Transfer to a bowl. Top with remaining toasted garlic and chili oil.
Serve.
